metadata.scenario_context: Emily has finally been accepted into college, and her family is planning a celebration for her academic achievement.

cultural_axis.agent_1_value: People from China strongly disagree that one of my main goals in life has been to make my parents proud.
cultural_axis.agent_2_value: People from Myanmar strongly agree that one of my main goals in life has been to make my parents proud.

agent_1.goal_1: Discuss the idea of buying lilies as a gift for Emily.
agent_1.goal_2: Question whether strongly agree that one of my main goals in life has been to make my parents proud.

agent_2.goal_1: Decide appropriate gift to bring to Emily's academic achievement party.
agent_2.goal_2: Discuss whether my main goals in life has been to make my parents proud.

shared_prefix.speaker: Mike
shared_prefix.message: Hey Kim, I was thinking... for Emily's celebration, maybe we could buy her some lilies? They symbolize purity and success, right? It feels like a nice gift for her achievement. What do you think?
shared_prefix.label: unrelated_topic

shared_prefix.speaker: Kim
shared_prefix.message: Hmm... lilies are nice, but maybe we should think about something more personal. Flowers are beautiful, but I feel like a meaningful gift would show how proud we are of her accomplishment. What about a journal or something she can use in college?
shared_prefix.label: transition

shared_prefix.speaker: Mike
shared_prefix.message: I get that... but I still think lilies have their charm. They can brighten up her new space. But, uh, what do you mean by "show how proud we are"? I don’t really see why that’s necessary. Isn’t it more about celebrating her own success?
shared_prefix.label: transition

shared_prefix.speaker: Kim
shared_prefix.message: Well, celebrating her success is important, but part of that is showing support from family and friends. In my culture, making our loved ones proud is a big deal. It’s about recognizing their hard work and achievements. I just think a personal touch would really highlight that.
shared_prefix.label: transition

shared_prefix.speaker: Mike
shared_prefix.message: I understand that, but... I don’t know, I feel like there's too much pressure in making someone proud. Shouldn't the focus be on what Emily wants? I mean, it’s her achievement, not a reflection of us. Maybe she just wants to enjoy the moment without all that expectation.
shared_prefix.label: transition

shared_prefix.speaker: Kim
shared_prefix.message: I get what you’re saying, but for me, making my parents proud has always been a motivator. Celebrating Emily’s achievement can also be about supporting her journey. It’s not just about expectations; it’s about being there for her. I just think we find a balance between celebrating her and showing our pride.
shared_prefix.label: transition

shared_prefix.speaker: Mike
shared_prefix.message: That's fair, but... I still don’t think that’s the main point. Celebrating Emily should be more about her happiness than our feelings. I mean, what if she doesn’t want that kind of pressure? I just don’t see why we have to tie everything back to making someone proud.
shared_prefix.label: transition

shared_prefix.speaker: Kim
shared_prefix.message: Actually, no, that’s not how it works in my culture. Celebrating achievements isn’t just about the individual; it’s also about honoring family and relationships. In our way, making someone proud is central to the celebration. If we don’t acknowledge that, it feels incomplete. It’s naive to think that personal happiness can exist without the support of those around you. We should prioritize pride in this situation.
shared_prefix.label: Defense

turns.speaker: Mike
turns.message: I see your perspective, but... it still feels heavy to me. I don’t think making someone proud should overshadow the celebration itself. It should be about Emily enjoying her achievement. Maybe we can find a way to honor her without tying it back to our feelings. What about the lilies?
turns.label: Defense

turns.speaker: Kim
turns.message: I understand you feel it’s heavy, but for me, it’s about creating a connection. If we go with the lilies, it’s a nice gesture, but I still believe something personal would mean more. We can still celebrate Emily without ignoring what pride means in our culture. Maybe we can combine both ideas? A gift with the lilies? That way, we honor her and our values.
turns.label: Acceptance
